task_text: Pendulum energy relay: A passive pendulum (a rod with a ball-shaped bob) hangs between the two arms, each of which holds a flat paddle. The left arm must actively push the pendulum so that it swings out toward the right arm. The right arm must catch it while it is still swinging fast and brake it, taking at least 60 % of its swing energy out, then actively drive it back so that it swings out toward the left arm, no longer touching it. The left arm must then touch it again, and the pendulum must end up hanging almost straight down and almost still, and stay that way for one second without the right paddle touching it. Phases, in order: left_excitation: the left paddle (any part of panda-0's tool link) touches the pendulum while that tool's centre-of-mass speed is above 0.03 m/s (an active push, recorded once); after that, the pendulum swings out toward the right arm beyond `minimum_excursion` = 0.18 rad (about 10.3 deg) from straight down, i.e. hinge angle q < -0.18 rad, bob displaced toward +x. The paddle may or may not still be touching the pendulum at that moment.; right_braking: the right paddle catches the swinging pendulum and brakes it. A catch starts at a step where the right paddle (any part of panda-1's tool link) touches the pendulum, the left paddle does not, the right paddle did not touch it on the previous physics step (a contact onset), and the pendulum's angular speed on the previous step was at least `brake_min_speed` = 1.0 rad/s; the swing energy E of that previous step is recorded. A catch is void once the left paddle touches the pendulum or more than `brake_window` = 0.5 s have passed since its start; a new catch then needs a new onset. The phase completes at a step during a valid catch where the right paddle touches the pendulum, its angular speed is below 0.45 rad/s, and its swing energy is at most (1 - `brake_energy_drop`) = 0.4 times the recorded energy. The swing energy is E = M g d (1 - cos q) + 0.5 I (dq/dt)^2, relative to hanging at rest, with the swinging link's mass M, the distance d of its centre of mass from the hinge axis and its moment of inertia I about that axis (the simulator's mass properties of the rod and bob).; right_return_impulse: the right paddle touches the pendulum while that tool's centre-of-mass speed is above 0.03 m/s (an active push, recorded once in this phase); after that, at a moment when the right paddle is not touching the pendulum, the pendulum is beyond `return_excursion` = 0.12 rad (about 6.9 deg) toward the left arm (q > 0.12 rad, bob displaced toward -x) and is still swinging further toward the left arm at more than 0.25 rad/s (dq/dt > +0.25 rad/s).; left_recovery: the left paddle touches the pendulum (any contact).; low_energy_hold: the pendulum is within 0.055 rad (about 3.2 deg) of hanging straight down (|q| < 0.055 rad) its angular speed is below 0.12 rad/s, and the right paddle does not touch it, for 1.0 s without interruption. The left paddle may touch it during the hold. This completes the task.
